title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East (early show) on 1970-02-11
source: SBD MR > DAT (disc 1 and first part of Star, last part lovelight via a DAT transfer so is not from circ. source); MAR > ? > R @ 3 @ ips. (aud patch source used in Dark Star and Lovelight); SBD MR > A77 > A77@ 71/2 ips (primary source for disc 2); Transfer info:  Akai GX636 direct tape head output  > Bottlehead tube tape pre pair Tesla tubes circa 1980  > Apogee Mini Me 24/96  > Apogee Mini DAC monitoring and mastering  > FLAC

ai_review.summary: High‑quality soundboard composite captures standout Cold Rain and Dark Star jams, though a mono‑channel issue on Uncle John’s requires a switch.
ai_review.review: This SBD composite is regarded as the best source for the February ’70 Fillmore East shows, delivering clear overall balance with only a brief one‑channel segment that benefits from a mono setting. Musically the night shines with an electrifying Cold Rain jam and a first‑half Dark Star that many fans cite as highlights, while Lovelight drags later in the set. The recording’s historical value outweighs its minor technical quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: Strong musical moments and a generally solid soundboard source, offset by some channel‑balance issues and uneven set quality.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Overall clear and well‑balanced; Uncle John's segment is recorded in one channel (use mono switch). Considered the best‑ever composite of these shows despite minor EQ/balance variations in other sources.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Two‑show night with an early partial set and a later full set after opening acts (Love, Allman Brothers, Peter Green). The flow is historic rather than flawless, with strong jams in the middle and a less focused closing jam.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Mentioned as part of the one‑guitar segment on Uncle John's; no specific praise or critique.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for his inventive bass work during the Cold Rain jam.
